sections.html:
Virginia's far southwestern corner, in the Appalachian coalfields beside Kentucky, is where Wise County lies. The seat is the town of Wise, and the biggest town is Big Stone Gap. Its 405 square miles are mountainous and almost entirely land, taking in High Knob, Powell Valley and a portion of the Jefferson National Forest.

Norton, an independent city, is surrounded by the county but is not part of it. Owners of Norton houses should use the city's offices instead of the county offices described below.

The count was 36,130 in 2020 and an estimated 34,824 in 2025, a drop from 41,452 in 2010. Of 16,644 housing units in 2020, 13.7% were vacant, and 70.4% of occupied units were owner-occupied. With numbers like that, empty and inherited houses are a regular topic.

Wise County has six incorporated towns: Appalachia, Big Stone Gap, Coeburn, Pound, St. Paul and Wise. Census-designated places include Big Stone Gap East, Dunbar, East Stone Gap, Osaka, Riverview, Stonega and Tacoma, plus the campus of the University of Virginia's College at Wise.

Plenty of owners live in unincorporated places like Derby, Dooley, Exeter, Imboden, Inman, Pardee, Roda and Virginia City, where only the county taxes the property. Inside a town there may be town offices too. Before setting a closing date, ask town hall what applies.

Property tax is split between two county offices, both in the town of Wise. One assesses and the other collects: the Commissioner of the Revenue values real estate, and the Treasurer sends bills and takes payment.

OfficeAddressPhoneHours
Commissioner of the Revenue206 E Main Street, Rooms 224 and 226, Wise, VA 24293 (mail: PO Box 1278)276-328-3556Monday to Friday, 8:30 am to 4:30 pm
Treasurer260 E Main Street, Room 240, Wise, VA 24293 (mail: PO Box 1308)276-328-4077Monday to Friday, 8 am to 4:30 pm, closed noon to 1

Property records for assessment are kept in the Commissioner's real estate department, which coordinates with the Circuit Court clerk and the Treasurer. Parcel details are searchable online in the county's EagleWeb Assessments tool. The State Corporation Commission or the Department of Taxation assesses railroads, pipelines and utility property, then reports to the Commissioner.

The 2026 rate is $0.69 for each $100 of assessed value, and the Board of Supervisors sets it every spring while working on the budget. The two due dates are June 10 and November 10. Your own bill is on the county parcel search.

  • Two bills a year go to whoever owned the property on January 1.
  • On June 11 and November 11 a 10% late penalty is added.
  • Interest begins July 1 and December 1, in that order.
  • A postmark on or before June 10 or November 10 keeps you on time.
  • A bill that never arrived is not a defense against penalty or interest.

Where a lender pays your tax, the county sends it a request, provided the tax ticket names the lender. If not, forwarding the bill is your job.

sections.h2: How do I appeal an assessment or correct an error?
sections.html:
Your first call is to the Commissioner of the Revenue, whose office holds the records and fields assessment questions. The county's real estate page links to a reassessment FAQ. Ask how often the county reassesses and when the appeal windows open this cycle.

Mistakes have a separate route in state law. Va. Code 58.1-3980 lets anyone aggrieved by a local assessment apply to the commissioner of the revenue for a correction, either within three years of the last day of the tax year or within a year of the assessment date, whichever comes later. For real estate it reaches commissioner errors and factual errors by others made during a general reassessment.

Forms for land use assessment and for tax relief are posted by the county too, covering seniors, people with disabilities and surviving spouses of disabled or fallen service members. Selling a house a surviving spouse lived in? Ask whether relief was applied.

Because the bill follows the owner of record on January 1, a mid-year sale does not automatically shift it to the buyer. The settlement sheet is where the tax is straightened out. Before you sign, have the closing office confirm these points with the Treasurer:

  • Is the June 10 half paid, and is the November 10 half still open?
  • Has a 10% penalty or interest been added to an unpaid half?
  • Who covers the months the buyer will own, given that the bill follows the owner of record?
  • For an inherited house, has the deed, will or list of heirs been recorded? The county relies on circuit court clerk records to update ownership.

Notify the Treasurer of any ownership or billing address change. A cash buyer can frequently purchase an inherited house with unpaid tax as is and clear the balance from the sale. The offer comes in writing, and accepting is your choice.

Preparation takes an afternoon. First, find your parcel on the county's search tool and confirm the owner named matches the deed. Second, call the Treasurer's office at 276-328-4077 and ask which halves of the current year are paid. Third, collect whatever shows who may sign: the deed, a will, or the list of heirs. Fourth, write down what is wrong with the house, from the roof to the plumbing, so a buyer's offer reflects the real condition.

Mail matters too. Send any change of address to the Treasurer so a final bill is not lost, since a missing bill does not cancel a penalty. If the house has been empty, check that the billing address on file is one you actually read.

With that in hand, you can compare a cash offer with the cost of repairs and the months a listing might take, and decide without pressure.

sections.h2: What a cash sale looks like in Wise County
sections.html:
Coal has driven the local economy since the 1880s, and housing demand still tracks jobs. Families move away or a parent dies, and the house stays empty. That is an ordinary story in this county. Cash buyers can take such a house in the condition it is in, which helps if repairs would cost more than you care to spend.

Commute and schools come up with buyers. The main roads are U.S. Route 23, U.S. Route 58 Alternate, and State Routes 63, 72 and 83. For high schools, the county has Union High in the west, Central High in the central and northern parts, and Eastside High in the east. Knowing these lets you describe the area plainly, and mentioning High Knob and the Clinch River trails never hurts.

faqs.q: When are Wise County real estate taxes due?
faqs.a: On June 10 and November 10. The next day brings a 10% penalty, and interest follows on July 1 and December 1.

faqs.q: What is the 2026 real estate tax rate in Wise County?
faqs.a: It is $0.69 per $100 of assessed value, set by the Board of Supervisors each spring as part of the budget.

faqs.q: Who sends the property tax bill in Wise County?
faqs.a: The Treasurer. The Commissioner of the Revenue sets the assessment, and the bill is addressed to the January 1 owner of record.

faqs.q: Is Norton part of Wise County for property tax?
faqs.a: No. Norton is an independent city within the county's borders but separate from it, so take Norton questions to the city.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Wise County house that has back taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. The back tax, plus a 10% penalty and interest, should be paid or settled at closing. The Treasurer can give the exact balance, and your closing office can explain handling.
